Rome and the Catholic Electorate

The ministries are installed in Rome, but possession of the capital has not reconciled the Holy See to the kingdom. Catholic associations debate participation in national politics while the crown insists on civil sovereignty. A patient administrative settlement must coexist with a continuing religious dispute.
Rome and the Catholic Electorate: concluded
Rome and the Catholic Electorate: presented
Maintain civil authority and the guarantees.
Encourage practical local accommodation.
Equip the National Capital: Preparatory Works
Equip the National Capital
Prepare offices, records and services for the national administration in Rome. Building a capital also exposes public finance to contractors and property speculation.
Equip the National Capital: enacted
Equip the National Capital: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Equip the National Capital: In Operation: concluded
Equip the National Capital: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
The Cabinet and the Railway Question

Railway policy and the demands of fiscal consolidation are dividing the parliamentary majority. The crown can seek another conservative ministry committed to retrenchment, or leave room for an opposition programme. A change of ministers cannot itself balance the treasury.
The Cabinet and the Railway Question: concluded
The Cabinet and the Railway Question: presented
Seek a ministry of fiscal consolidation.
Open negotiations with the opposition.
The Parliamentary Revolution

The Historical Left offers a broader reform programme as the old governing coalition fractures over railways and taxation. Depretis seeks support among deputies who favor education and a wider electorate. This is a parliamentary realignment, not a social revolution.
The Parliamentary Revolution: concluded
The Parliamentary Revolution: presented
Entrust the reform programme to the Left.
Retain a conservative parliamentary ministry.
Implement the Coppino School Programme: Preparatory Works
Implement the Coppino School Programme

Strengthen compulsory elementary attendance through municipal grants, trained teachers and inspections. Rural poverty and uneven local resources remain barriers to attendance even after the law is adopted.
Implement the Coppino School Programme: enacted
Implement the Coppino School Programme: In Operation

Municipal inspectors and teachers are beginning their work. Attendance obligations now have practical support, but literacy will develop through schooling rather than an immediate administrative decree.
Implement the Coppino School Programme: In Operation: concluded
Implement the Coppino School Programme: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Broaden the Electoral Franchise
Lower the fiscal barriers to parliamentary participation. The proposed electorate remains limited, with literacy and economic qualifications still excluding much of the population.
Broaden the Electoral Franchise: enacted
Trasformismo and the Governing Majority

Depretis invites moderate deputies across the old party divide to sustain a broad parliamentary centre. The arrangement can stabilize legislation, but bargaining over patronage risks blurring responsibility and weakening effective opposition.
Trasformismo and the Governing Majority: concluded
Trasformismo and the Governing Majority: presented
Build a broad parliamentary centre.
Defend clearer government and opposition lines.
Negotiate Railway Operating Conventions: Preparatory Works
Negotiate Railway Operating Conventions

Reorganize the management of the railway networks through operating conventions and public supervision. This concerns administration and investment commitments, not the instant construction of tracks.
Negotiate Railway Operating Conventions: enacted
Negotiate Railway Operating Conventions: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Negotiate Railway Operating Conventions: In Operation: concluded
Negotiate Railway Operating Conventions: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Support Industrial Rubber and Technical Training: Preparatory Works
Support Industrial Rubber and Technical Training

Milanese entrepreneurs are developing rubber goods and engineering workshops. Encourage skilled workers and industrial research without assuming that a small new enterprise already possesses a mass-production tire industry.
Support Industrial Rubber and Technical Training: enacted
Support Industrial Rubber and Technical Training: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Support Industrial Rubber and Technical Training: In Operation: concluded
Support Industrial Rubber and Technical Training: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Support Electric Lighting in Milan: Preparatory Works
Support Electric Lighting in Milan

Back municipal contracts and engineering work for an electric supply around the city centre. The Santa Radegonda initiative represents an early local network, with heavy dependence on machinery, finance and reliable operation.
Support Electric Lighting in Milan: enacted
Support Electric Lighting in Milan: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Support Electric Lighting in Milan: In Operation: concluded
Support Electric Lighting in Milan: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Support Strategic Steelmaking at Terni: Preparatory Works
Support Strategic Steelmaking at Terni

Place public contracts for armor and heavy engineering with the emerging steel industry in Umbria. Naval independence demands capital and technical skill as well as furnaces, and the contracts tie public finance to industrial development.
Support Strategic Steelmaking at Terni: enacted
Support Strategic Steelmaking at Terni: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Support Strategic Steelmaking at Terni: In Operation: concluded
Support Strategic Steelmaking at Terni: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Fund Brin's Naval Industrial Programme: Preparatory Works
Fund Brin's Naval Industrial Programme

Coordinate naval design, heavy machinery and armor procurement. The fleet must share the treasury with education, transport and public health, while ships still need to be ordered and built through the normal yards.
Fund Brin's Naval Industrial Programme: enacted
Fund Brin's Naval Industrial Programme: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Fund Brin's Naval Industrial Programme: In Operation: concluded
Fund Brin's Naval Industrial Programme: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Support Turin's Motor Engineering Workshops: Preparatory Works
Support Turin's Motor Engineering Workshops

A new group of investors is organizing automobile manufacture in Turin. Experimental workshops and trained engineers can establish a promising foundation, but motor transport remains a small and uncertain business.
Support Turin's Motor Engineering Workshops: enacted
Support Turin's Motor Engineering Workshops: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Support Turin's Motor Engineering Workshops: In Operation: concluded
Support Turin's Motor Engineering Workshops: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Cholera in Naples

An epidemic has exposed the dangers of overcrowding and inadequate water and drainage in Naples. Municipal officials demand a sustained public-health response. Emergency assistance can relieve distress, but rebuilding urban services requires a separate funded programme.
Cholera in Naples: concluded
Cholera in Naples: presented
Coordinate relief through the municipality.
Leave the immediate response to local institutions.
Rebuild Naples' Water and Sanitation: Preparatory Works
Rebuild Naples' Water and Sanitation
Finance drainage, water supply and municipal engineering after the epidemic. Urban renewal must be supervised to limit speculation and the displacement of poor households.
Rebuild Naples' Water and Sanitation: enacted
Rebuild Naples' Water and Sanitation: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Rebuild Naples' Water and Sanitation: In Operation: concluded
Rebuild Naples' Water and Sanitation: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Protection or Export Markets?

Industrialists and grain producers press for stronger protection. Exporters of wine, oil, citrus and silk warn that trading partners may retaliate. Ministers must choose which interests to support rather than treating a tariff as a benefit to every branch of production.
Protection or Export Markets?: concluded
Protection or Export Markets?: presented
Back industrial and grain protection.
Preserve access to foreign markets.
A Customs Dispute with France

French commercial interests have answered our protectionist course with pressure of their own. Exporting districts face a loss of markets. Retaining the tariff preserves favored domestic interests, while compromise can reduce the confrontation.
A Customs Dispute with France: concluded
A Customs Dispute with France: presented
Maintain the tariff despite the dispute.
Seek a commercial compromise.
After Depretis

The death of Depretis closes a long period of parliamentary management. Crispi argues for a more forceful executive and an assertive foreign policy. The crown can support his programme or preserve a more restrained parliamentary balance.
After Depretis: concluded
After Depretis: presented
Give Crispi a parliamentary mandate.
Support a ministry of parliamentary restraint.
Bring the Zanardelli Code into Force

Adopt a common liberal criminal code, abolishing the death penalty in ordinary criminal law and distinguishing peaceful labor action from criminal violence. Military law and the practical use of police power remain separate questions.
Bring the Zanardelli Code into Force: enacted
The Cost of an Assertive Ministry

Military expenditure and disputes within the parliamentary majority have weakened Crispi's position. The crown must choose between seeking a different coalition and retaining an increasingly contested executive.
The Cost of an Assertive Ministry: concluded
The Cost of an Assertive Ministry: presented
Seek a new parliamentary majority.
Retain the ministry.
Labor Organizes at Genoa

Socialist organizers seek a national political party alongside trade unions and local associations. Their movement is not identical to anarchism or every rural protest. The government can tolerate lawful organization or rely more heavily on police surveillance.
Labor Organizes at Genoa: concluded
Labor Organizes at Genoa: presented
Protect lawful political organization.
Expand political surveillance.
The Banca Romana Scandal

Investigations into the note issue and property lending of the Banca Romana have exposed irregular accounts and damaging political connections. Confidence in the issuing banks is shaken. An open inquiry risks ministers' reputations, while concealment leaves the financial problem unresolved.
The Banca Romana Scandal: concluded
The Banca Romana Scandal: presented
Open a parliamentary inquiry.
Contain the inquiry within the ministry.
Reorganize the Issuing Banks: Preparatory Works
Reorganize the Issuing Banks

Create a consolidated Bank of Italy from the Banca Nazionale and the two Tuscan issuing banks, liquidate the Banca Romana and strengthen supervision. The banks of Naples and Sicily retain their distinct issuing privileges under the new settlement.
Reorganize the Issuing Banks: enacted
Reorganize the Issuing Banks: In Operation

The banking reorganization has entered operation. Supervision and consolidated reserves offer a firmer foundation, while the southern issuing banks remain distinct. The reform does not remove the political responsibility exposed by the scandal.
Reorganize the Issuing Banks: In Operation: concluded
Reorganize the Issuing Banks: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
The Scandal Reaches the Cabinet

The banking inquiry has compromised the government's authority. Crispi offers a return to strong executive direction, while other deputies demand a ministry tied more closely to parliamentary scrutiny.
The Scandal Reaches the Cabinet: concluded
The Scandal Reaches the Cabinet: presented
Recall Crispi to form a ministry.
Seek a ministry committed to scrutiny.
The Fasci Siciliani

Peasant leagues, miners and urban workers are organizing around rents, wages and local taxation. Their grievances differ from the legitimist resistance of the unification years. Landowners demand protection, while the leagues seek recognition and arbitration.
The Fasci Siciliani: concluded
The Fasci Siciliani: presented
Recognize the grievances and begin mediation.
Treat the leagues as a public-order threat.
The Sicilian Emergency

The cabinet has chosen coercion against the Sicilian leagues. Military jurisdiction and arrests may break their public organization, but suppression will not settle the underlying conflicts over land and work. Ministers can still retreat toward civil mediation.
The Sicilian Emergency: concluded
The Sicilian Emergency: presented
Authorize exceptional military administration.
Return the dispute to civil mediation.
Establish Agrarian Arbitration in Sicily: Preparatory Works
Establish Agrarian Arbitration in Sicily

Create civil offices to mediate leases, wages and local grievances. A settlement must face both organized workers and influential landowners, and cannot promise the disappearance of agrarian conflict.
Establish Agrarian Arbitration in Sicily: enacted
Establish Agrarian Arbitration in Sicily: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Establish Agrarian Arbitration in Sicily: In Operation: concluded
Establish Agrarian Arbitration in Sicily: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Dear Bread and the Cities

Urban households are struggling with expensive bread and political tension. Local demonstrations demand relief, while officials fear that gatherings will spread beyond their control. Emergency food policy and military policing offer sharply different responses.
Dear Bread and the Cities: concluded
Dear Bread and the Cities: presented
Prioritize food relief and civil negotiation.
Place public order in military hands.
The Milan Military Repression

The military emergency has ended in lethal repression of the demonstrations. Reports of force against civilians have deepened the political crisis. The crown must decide whether to defend the command publicly or demand an inquiry.
The Milan Military Repression: concluded
The Milan Military Repression: presented
Publicly endorse the military command.
Order an inquiry into the use of force.
The Public Security Bills

Pelloux's supporters seek exceptional restrictions on the press, meetings and political organization. Opponents challenge the attempt to govern through emergency powers. The conflict tests the practical boundaries of the Statuto and parliamentary government.
The Public Security Bills: concluded
The Public Security Bills: presented
Press the exceptional legislation.
Defend parliamentary procedure and compromise.
A Return to Parliamentary Government

Opposition to exceptional measures has made the governing majority untenable. The crown can withdraw the restrictions and seek a ministry within ordinary parliamentary practice. The dispute leaves a lasting question about the monarchy's political role.
A Return to Parliamentary Government: concluded
A Return to Parliamentary Government: presented
Withdraw the exceptional measures.
Persist with the exceptional course.
The Death of Victor Emmanuel II

Victor Emmanuel II has died. Umberto succeeds to a kingdom whose institutions extend far beyond the old Sardinian state, but regional divisions and the Roman Question remain unsettled. The succession preserves the monarchy's legal continuity.
The Death of Victor Emmanuel II: concluded
The Death of Victor Emmanuel II: presented
Recognize Umberto as king.
The Attempt on the King at Naples

An attacker has attempted to strike the king during a public appearance in Naples. The attempt has failed. Ministers debate whether the incident justifies broad political policing or should be handled through ordinary criminal proceedings.
The Attempt on the King at Naples: concluded
The Attempt on the King at Naples: presented
Proceed under ordinary criminal law.
Expand precautions around the crown.
Another Attempt on Umberto

Another attack on the king has failed. Police officials demand wider preventive powers, while critics warn against making political opinion itself a crime. The crown's security and the limits of public authority again meet in the courts.
Another Attempt on Umberto: concluded
Another Attempt on Umberto: presented
Let the courts try the attacker.
Strengthen preventive policing.
The Assassination of Umberto I

Umberto has been assassinated at Monza by Gaetano Bresci. The killing ends the reign amid bitter disputes about public order and the crown's place in politics. Victor Emmanuel III succeeds under the existing constitutional settlement.
The Assassination of Umberto I: concluded
The Assassination of Umberto I: presented
Maintain the constitutional succession.
Rerum Novarum and the Social Question

The papal encyclical addresses labor, property and the responsibilities of employers and public authority. Catholic social associations find new grounds for organization. Its publication does not resolve the Roman Question or turn church and state into a single institution.
Rerum Novarum and the Social Question: concluded
Rerum Novarum and the Social Question: presented
Allow the social debate to develop.
Strengthen Consular Protection for Emigrants: Preparatory Works
Strengthen Consular Protection for Emigrants

Expand the capacity of consulates to advise emigrants, investigate abuses by agents and maintain contact with communities abroad. This protects people who move through the normal migration system, rather than directing entire populations to colonial settlements.
Strengthen Consular Protection for Emigrants: enacted
Strengthen Consular Protection for Emigrants: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Strengthen Consular Protection for Emigrants: In Operation: concluded
Strengthen Consular Protection for Emigrants: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Develop the Royal Southern Dockyards: Preparatory Works
Develop the Royal Southern Dockyards

Coordinate the yards of Naples, Palermo and Messina with technical schools and suppliers. A maritime monarchy requires trained engineers and sustained contracts, not merely a claim to a naval tradition.
Develop the Royal Southern Dockyards: enacted
Develop the Royal Southern Dockyards: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Develop the Royal Southern Dockyards: In Operation: concluded
Develop the Royal Southern Dockyards: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Establish Royal Agrarian Credit Offices: Preparatory Works
Establish Royal Agrarian Credit Offices
Offer supervised credit and mediation to tenants and small cultivators. The crown must confront local patronage and the influence of large landowners if reform is to reach the countryside.
Establish Royal Agrarian Credit Offices: enacted
Establish Royal Agrarian Credit Offices: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Establish Royal Agrarian Credit Offices: In Operation: concluded
Establish Royal Agrarian Credit Offices: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
The Crown and the Provinces

Unification has brought distinct legal traditions and regional elites under the Bourbon crown. Provincial compacts may secure cooperation at the expense of central uniformity. Royal prefectures promise firmer administration but expose the dynasty to resistance against central control.
The Crown and the Provinces: concluded
The Crown and the Provinces: presented
Negotiate provincial fiscal compacts.
Strengthen the royal prefectures.
Contract Mediterranean Mail and Steamship Services: Preparatory Works
Contract Mediterranean Mail and Steamship Services

Connect southern ports and existing overseas stations through regular commercial contracts. Subsidies may strengthen maritime services, but distant settlements still require security, employment and willing migrants.
Contract Mediterranean Mail and Steamship Services: enacted
Contract Mediterranean Mail and Steamship Services: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Contract Mediterranean Mail and Steamship Services: In Operation: concluded
Contract Mediterranean Mail and Steamship Services: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Create a Royal Emigrant Protection Service: Preparatory Works
Create a Royal Emigrant Protection Service
The maritime crown can assist emigrants through port inspections and consular representation. Overseas ambitions do not remove rural poverty or oblige families to settle in royal possessions.
Create a Royal Emigrant Protection Service: enacted
Create a Royal Emigrant Protection Service: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Create a Royal Emigrant Protection Service: In Operation: concluded
Create a Royal Emigrant Protection Service: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Catholic Associations and the Royal Social Policy

Catholic associations call for practical action on working conditions, mutual aid and rural poverty. Royal patronage can support these institutions, but landowners and industrial employers remain powerful interests within the monarchy.
Catholic Associations and the Royal Social Policy: concluded
Catholic Associations and the Royal Social Policy: presented
Recognize lawful mutual-aid associations.
Keep social initiatives under close royal patronage.
The Reduced Milling Duty
Begin the Reduction of the Milling Duty
Reduce the burden of the milling tax while preparing its eventual repeal. The cabinet must replace the lost receipts or accept a tighter budget for its other programmes.
Begin the Reduction of the Milling Duty: enacted
The Milling Duty Is Abolished
The staged reduction of the milling duty has reached its conclusion. Abolition removes an unpopular burden on staple food, but the treasury can no longer rely on its receipts.
The Milling Duty Is Abolished: concluded
The Milling Duty Is Abolished: presented
Complete the repeal.
The Consolidation of Public Finance

The treasury has accumulated a substantial reserve under a policy of fiscal restraint. Ministers can recognize this achievement without treating a reserve as proof that every future budget will balance. New commitments will compete for the funds already gathered.
The Consolidation of Public Finance: concluded
The Consolidation of Public Finance: presented
Preserve a prudent fiscal course.

France Establishes Itself in Tunisia

French control of Tunisia has narrowed Italy's room for maneuver in the central Mediterranean. Commercial communities and naval planners demand an answer. Closer relations with the continental powers offer one response, while accommodation with France remains possible.
France Establishes Itself in Tunisia: concluded
France Establishes Itself in Tunisia: presented
Explore a continental diplomatic alignment.
Seek accommodation with France.
Propose the Triple Alliance

Seek a continental agreement with Germany and Austria. Both governments must consent. The historical defensive understanding leaves the Austrian frontier dispute unresolved and does not promise support for a confrontation with Britain.
Propose the Triple Alliance: enacted
An Italian Proposal for a Continental Agreement

Italy seeks an agreement with Germany and Austria. Participation may deter rivals, but it also creates obligations toward a state with its own Mediterranean ambitions and unresolved frontier grievances. Each prospective partner retains the right to refuse.
An Italian Proposal for a Continental Agreement: concluded
An Italian Proposal for a Continental Agreement: presented
Consent to the proposed agreement.
Decline the agreement.
An Italian Proposal for a Continental Agreement

Italy seeks an agreement with Germany and Austria. Participation may deter rivals, but it also creates obligations toward a state with its own Mediterranean ambitions and unresolved frontier grievances. Each prospective partner retains the right to refuse.
An Italian Proposal for a Continental Agreement: concluded
An Italian Proposal for a Continental Agreement: presented
Consent to the proposed agreement.
Decline the agreement.
The Continental Agreement Is Ratified

Germany and Austria have both accepted the proposal. Italy joins their alliance while retaining its unresolved frontier interests. The agreement rests on continuing diplomatic cooperation, and the cabinet will review its position when the initial term expires.
The Continental Agreement Is Ratified: concluded
The Continental Agreement Is Ratified: presented
Ratify the agreement.
The Continental Negotiations Close
The negotiations have ended without a joint agreement. A refusal, a change of circumstances or the expiry of the talks has prevented ratification. No alliance has been created by the proposal.
The Continental Negotiations Close: concluded
The Continental Negotiations Close: presented
Close the negotiations.
Reviewing the Continental Commitment

The original diplomatic term has elapsed. Austria remains both a partner and a potential rival on the Italian frontier. The cabinet can sustain the alliance if relations still permit it, or withdraw from the arrangements it accepted.
Reviewing the Continental Commitment: concluded
Reviewing the Continental Commitment: presented
Continue cooperation where the alliances survive.
Withdraw from the continental commitment.
Purchase the Assab Establishment

Seek a sovereign coastal establishment from the Afar government. The earlier Rubattino venture was a private commercial arrangement. State acquisition requires a separate agreement and does not entitle Italy to the Eritrean hinterland.
Purchase the Assab Establishment: enacted
Purchase the Assab Establishment: Awaiting a Reply
An Italian Proposal Concerning the Port

Italian representatives offer payment for the specified coastal establishment. Acceptance transfers that port alone. Refusal preserves sovereignty and returns the deposited funds to the Italian government.
An Italian Proposal Concerning the Port: concluded
An Italian Proposal Concerning the Port: presented
Accept the limited transfer.
Retain sovereignty over the port.
Purchase the Assab Establishment: Agreement Concluded

The local government has accepted the agreement and the transfer has been completed. Administration must now be organized for the port. The agreement conveys no automatic title to neighboring districts.
Purchase the Assab Establishment: Agreement Concluded: concluded
Purchase the Assab Establishment: Agreement Concluded: presented
Receive the coastal establishment.
Purchase the Assab Establishment: Negotiations Closed
The proposal has expired or been declined. The reserved funds are returned where the negotiation remained outstanding. Any later acquisition must follow a new diplomatic or military course.
Purchase the Assab Establishment: Negotiations Closed: concluded
Purchase the Assab Establishment: Negotiations Closed: presented
Close the file.
British Consultation over Massawa
Consult Britain over Massawa
Discuss a limited Italian establishment at Massawa with Britain before approaching Egypt. British consent offers diplomatic cover but cannot by itself transfer Egyptian sovereignty.
Consult Britain over Massawa: enacted
Italy Seeks British Support in the Red Sea

Italy proposes to negotiate for Massawa. London can consent to the approach or oppose it. Egypt must still decide whether to transfer the port, and the understanding does not authorize the annexation of neighboring African states.
Italy Seeks British Support in the Red Sea: concluded
Italy Seeks British Support in the Red Sea: presented
Accept a limited Italian approach.
Oppose an Italian establishment.
The British Position on Massawa

The consultation with Britain is concluded. Egyptian consent is still necessary before a port can change hands. If British support was withheld or the consultation expired, the proposed route remains closed.
The British Position on Massawa: concluded
The British Position on Massawa: presented
Record the diplomatic position.
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa
Offer Egypt a limited agreement for the port following British diplomatic consent. The proposal does not convey sovereignty over the neighboring highlands or authorize an advance into Ethiopia.
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa: enacted
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa: Awaiting a Reply
An Italian Proposal Concerning the Port

Italian representatives offer payment for the specified coastal establishment. Acceptance transfers that port alone. Refusal preserves sovereignty and returns the deposited funds to the Italian government.
An Italian Proposal Concerning the Port: concluded
An Italian Proposal Concerning the Port: presented
Accept the limited transfer.
Retain sovereignty over the port.
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa: Agreement Concluded

The local government has accepted the agreement and the transfer has been completed. Administration must now be organized for the port. The agreement conveys no automatic title to neighboring districts.
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa: Agreement Concluded: concluded
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa: Agreement Concluded: presented
Receive the coastal establishment.
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa: Negotiations Closed
The proposal has expired or been declined. The reserved funds are returned where the negotiation remained outstanding. Any later acquisition must follow a new diplomatic or military course.
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa: Negotiations Closed: concluded
Negotiate an Egyptian Transfer of Massawa: Negotiations Closed: presented
Close the file.
Organize the Eritrean Coastal Administration: Preparatory Works
Organize the Eritrean Coastal Administration

Coordinate the existing coastal possessions under a single colonial administration. The organization covers only districts already held by Italy. Ethiopian sovereignty and disputed frontiers require separate diplomacy or an actual war settlement.
Organize the Eritrean Coastal Administration: enacted
Organize the Eritrean Coastal Administration: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Organize the Eritrean Coastal Administration: In Operation: concluded
Organize the Eritrean Coastal Administration: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
Negotiate with the Ethiopian Court

Offer trade and diplomatic cooperation to the Ethiopian government. Ministers disagree over whether Italian mediation abroad should be optional or obligatory. The Ethiopian court must answer, and a treaty cannot simply be assumed to create a protectorate.
Negotiate with the Ethiopian Court: enacted
Negotiations with the Ethiopian Court
Italy Proposes a Diplomatic Treaty

Italy offers commercial cooperation and diplomatic mediation. The Ethiopian government may accept assistance while preserving its own relations with other powers, or reject the treaty altogether. Neither choice surrenders Ethiopian independence.
Italy Proposes a Diplomatic Treaty: concluded
Italy Proposes a Diplomatic Treaty: presented
Accept cooperation while preserving diplomatic independence.
Decline the proposed treaty.
The Disputed Meaning of the Ethiopian Treaty

The Ethiopian court understands Italian diplomatic assistance as optional. Advocates of expansion in Rome wish to treat it as an exclusive obligation. Respecting the Ethiopian reading preserves the agreement. An exclusive claim will provoke a diplomatic dispute rather than create a protectorate.
The Disputed Meaning of the Ethiopian Treaty: concluded
The Disputed Meaning of the Ethiopian Treaty: presented
Recognize independent Ethiopian diplomacy.
Assert an exclusive diplomatic claim.
Negotiations with Ethiopia End
The proposed agreement has been declined or has failed to reach a timely settlement. No protectorate or diplomatic obligation has been created.
Negotiations with Ethiopia End: concluded
Negotiations with Ethiopia End: presented
End the negotiations.
Reject the Italian Protectorate Claim

Italy has interpreted diplomatic assistance as an exclusive right to conduct Ethiopian foreign relations. The Ethiopian government rejects that interpretation and asserts its right to deal directly with other powers.
Reject the Italian Protectorate Claim: concluded
Reject the Italian Protectorate Claim: presented
Defend independent diplomacy.
Press the Disputed Ethiopian Claim
Prepare to enforce the rejected diplomatic claim. This creates a limited diplomatic pretext, not a conquered Ethiopia. Any war must be fought through the normal military and peace systems.
Press the Disputed Ethiopian Claim: enacted
The Ethiopian Campaign

Italy is now fighting Ethiopia. Distance, transport and supply constrain the expedition, while the Ethiopian government mobilizes to defend its independence. Political expectations in Rome do not determine the result in the field.
The Ethiopian Campaign: concluded
The Ethiopian Campaign: presented
Record the commitment of the expedition.
Support the Ethiopian Expedition: Preparatory Works
Support the Ethiopian Expedition
Improve transport and supply for the forces committed in the Horn of Africa. Preparations support the army without manufacturing a battle result or creating regiments outside normal recruitment.
Support the Ethiopian Expedition: enacted
Support the Ethiopian Expedition: In Operation
The funded preparations have been completed. The institutions can begin their work, although their success still depends on local administration, employment and the resources of the kingdom.
Support the Ethiopian Expedition: In Operation: concluded
Support the Ethiopian Expedition: In Operation: presented
Put the programme into operation.
A Reverse on the Eritrean Frontier

The expedition has encountered a serious operational reverse near the coastal frontier. Reports expose the danger of dispersed detachments and inadequate support. Ministers can reconsider inland ambitions or accept the political cost of continuing the campaign.
A Reverse on the Eritrean Frontier: concluded
A Reverse on the Eritrean Frontier: presented
Demand a review of the expedition.
Maintain the commitment despite the reverse.
After the Ethiopian War

The fighting with Ethiopia has ended. The settlement must be judged by the territory and independence actually retained, rather than by the cabinet's original claims. An independent Ethiopian government remains entitled to conduct its own diplomacy.
After the Ethiopian War: concluded
After the Ethiopian War: presented
Abandon the exclusive diplomatic claim.
Review the expedition without a new commitment.
An Ethiopian Protectorate Established by the Peace

The actual war settlement has placed Ethiopia under Italian protection. Such a position requires administration and cooperation with local institutions. A treaty claim alone could never have produced this result.
An Ethiopian Protectorate Established by the Peace: concluded
An Ethiopian Protectorate Established by the Peace: presented
Implement the actual settlement.
Negotiations with Hobyo
Negotiate a Protectorate with Hobyo

Offer a treaty preserving the local ruler and internal administration while placing foreign relations under Italian protection. The ruler can refuse. The agreement conveys no automatic sovereignty over neighboring communities.
Negotiate a Protectorate with Hobyo: enacted
An Italian Treaty Offer to Hobyo
